Would cache_fit() compute, or load?

Source: R/cache_would_fit.R
cache_would_fit.Rd

Answers, without computing anything, whether cache_fit called with the same arguments would run its computation. A job uses it to guard a resource, memory or cores, only when a fit will actually run, rather than refusing a session for a fit it would simply load from the cache.

Usage

cache_would_fit(
  name,
  code,
  seed = NULL,
  dir = study_dir("estimates"),
  refit = FALSE,
  packages = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Character(1). File stem; the result is stored at file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".rds")).

code

The computation: an inline call or {} block, or a variable holding a quoted call.

seed

NULL or a single whole number.

dir

Character(1). An existing directory. Defaults to the study's estimates folder.

refit

Logical(1). TRUE recomputes and overwrites the file only when it is stale or unkeyed; a valid cache is still loaded, not recomputed, regardless of refit.

packages

NULL or a character vector of package names whose versions are added to the key. Use it for a package that does the work beneath a wrapper and so never appears in code itself; see Details.

Value

TRUE if cache_fit() with the same arguments would run code, FALSE if it would load the cached result or stop on a stale or unkeyed file without computing.

Details

The arguments are cache_fit()'s, with the same names, order and defaults, and none is dropped: name and dir locate the file, code, seed and packages make the key, and refit decides what a stale or unkeyed file does. Write the call exactly as the cache_fit() call it guards, for example cache_would_fit("forest", rfsrc(f, data = d), seed = 1) before cache_fit("forest", rfsrc(f, data = d), seed = 1). code is captured as cache_fit() captures it, by substitution, and is never evaluated: inline code and a variable holding a quoted call both work, and an already-computed object is refused as it is there. The same rule about wrappers applies; see cache_fit.

The answer comes from the same internal decision cache_fit() makes, not from a copy of it, so the two cannot drift apart:

  • no file: TRUE;

  • a file whose key matches: FALSE, whatever refit is, because a valid cache is loaded even under refit = TRUE;

  • a stale file (the code, an input, the seed or a package version changed) or an unkeyed or unreadable file: TRUE with refit = TRUE, and FALSE without it.

The last case is deliberate. Without refit, cache_fit() stops on a stale or unkeyed file before it computes anything, so nothing will run and there is nothing to guard; the error that follows is cache_fit()'s to raise, with the list of what changed. For the same reason, an existing file under refit = FALSE is not read at all, since every outcome there computes nothing.

Arguments are checked as cache_fit() checks them, and a bad one raises the same error, naming cache_fit(), including a dir that does not exist. Under refit = TRUE an existing file is read to compare its key, so a matching fit is read here and again by cache_fit().

See also

cache_fit

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "cache-would-fit-example")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
x <- c(3, 1, 2)
cache_would_fit("sorted", sort(x), dir = dir)
#> [1] TRUE
fit <- cache_fit("sorted", sort(x), dir = dir)
cache_would_fit("sorted", sort(x), dir = dir)
#> [1] FALSE
x <- c(4, 1, 2)
cache_would_fit("sorted", sort(x), dir = dir)
#> [1] FALSE
cache_would_fit("sorted", sort(x), dir = dir, refit = TRUE)
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
